subject: Generating predictions from a space-time LGCP model

messages.author: b4e7ce05f3e73a6b
messages.subject: Generating predictions from a space-time LGCP model
parts:
Hi INLA users,

I am fitting a space-time log Gaussian Cox process model with covariates and am coming unstuck when trying to generate spatial predictions. I would like to generate a lot of predictions from this model, somewhere in the region of 24 different spatial predictions of the entire mesh.

Following the INLA tutorials I have tried to generate spatial predictions while fitting the model. I have appended a dataframe of covariate values from which I want to generate predictions and have included a column of NAs for the Y/ Frequency column. I have also specified link = 1 and compute = TRUE in the `control.predictor` argument.

The model runs fine when there is no prediction data, but when I include the NAs I get the following error:

file: smtp-taucs.c  hgid: 0bed76828f01  date: Tue Sep 03 11:21:49 2019 +0300
Function: GMRFLib_factorise_sparse_matrix_TAUCS(), Line: 876, Thread: 0
Fail to factorize Q. I will try to fix it...

Can anyone shed light on why I might be getting this error?

Following this post: http://www.r-inla.org/events/problemswithopenblas I have tried `inla.setOption(mkl = TRUE) but this does not resolve the issue.

Alternatively, given that I am planning on generating so many predicted surfaces should I try an alternative method to generate predictions? For example by sampling from the posterior instead?

Any help would be greatly appreciated!

Many thanks,

James


Here is my model set up. I am working on a Windows server with 44 cores and 512GB memory.

A.st <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh = smesh,
                         loc = smesh$loc[agg.dat$area, ],
                         group = agg.dat$season,
                         n.group = k,
                         mesh.group = tmesh)

idx <- inla.spde.make.index(name = 's',
                            n.spde = barrier.model$f$n,
                            n.group = k)

stk <- inla.stack(data = list(y = agg.dat$Freq,
                              exposure = agg.dat$exp_adj),
                  A = list(A.st, 1),
                  effects = list(idx,
                                 list(b0 = rep(1, nrow(agg.dat)),
                                      x_bar = agg.dat$x_bar,
                                      x_bar_c_s = agg.dat$x_bar_c_s,
                                      x_bar_c_s_m = agg.dat$x_bar_c_s_m,
                                      x_res_smy = agg.dat$x_res_smy)))

pcrho <- list(theta = list(prior = 'pccor1', param = c(.7, .7)))

f_1 <- y ~ -1 + b0 + x_bar + x_bar_c_s + x_bar_c_s_m + x_res_smy +
  f(s,
    model = barrier.model,
    group = s.group,
    replicate = s.repl,
    control.group = list(model = 'ar1',
                         hyper = pcrho))

m_1 <- inla(f_1,
            family = 'poisson', 
            data = inla.stack.data(stk),
            control.predictor = list(A = inla.stack.A(stk),
                                     link = 1,
                                     compute = TRUE),
            E = agg.dat$exp_adj,
            control.inla = list(strategy = "gaussian",
                                int.strategy = "eb"),
            control.compute = list(openmp.strategy = "huge",
                                   config = TRUE,
                                   dic = T,
                                   waic = T),
                        control.mode = list(theta = c(1.323, 7.089, 0.643), restart = T),
            verbose = T,
            num.threads = 16) # switch on when trialling

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Generating predictions from a space-time LGCP model
parts:
On Thu, 2019-10-31 at 09:56 -0700, James Grecian wrote:
> The model runs fine when there is no prediction data, but when I
> include the NAs I get the following error:
>
> file: smtp-taucs.c hgid: 0bed76828f01 date: Tue Sep 03 11:21:49
> 2019 +0300
> Function: GMRFLib_factorise_sparse_matrix_TAUCS(), Line: 876,
> Thread: 0
> Fail to factorize Q. I will try to fix it...
>
> Can anyone shed light on why I might be getting this error?

Hi.

this is an error saying that the precision matrix is numerical singular.
Doing prediction, this could happen more easily, as long term prediction
can get highly non-informative. So doing one-step ahead prediction is easier than
doing predictions one year ahead.

The way out is to re-check your model if you have intrinsic model
components (like rw1/rw2, etc), that tends to get 'more singular' without data,
and maybe use proper model components instead. Also check the fit, that the model components
have a reasonable posterior variance.


Let me know
H


--
Håvard Rue
Helpdesk
he...@r-inla.org

parts:
Looks like you’re using the wrong E value. I think you intended to use the “exposure” variable from the stack data (extract with inla.stack.data() before the inla call to make that more easily accessible). If this is a LGCP likelihood, I.e. with observations and exposure setup to construct a Cox point process likelihood, then it may be clearer to split into three sub stacks; one with y=1, one with y=0, and one with y=NA that only deals with the prediction.

Finn

On 31 Oct 2019, at 16:56, James Grecian <jamesg...@gmail.com> wrote:

﻿

Hi INLA users,

I am fitting a space-time log Gaussian Cox process model with covariates and am coming unstuck when trying to generate spatial predictions. I would like to generate a lot of predictions from this model, somewhere in the region of 24 different spatial predictions of the entire mesh.

Following the INLA tutorials I have tried to generate spatial predictions while fitting the model. I have appended a dataframe of covariate values from which I want to generate predictions and have included a column of NAs for the Y/ Frequency column. I have also specified link = 1 and compute = TRUE in the `control.predictor` argument.

The model runs fine when there is no prediction data, but when I include the NAs I get the following error:

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Generating predictions from a space-time LGCP model
parts:
Hi Finn,

You’re right this is an LGCP likelihood. I have a column for observations (Y) and a column for exposure. However I have different numbers of individuals sampled in each period, so the exposure has been adjusted to account for this effect (exp_adj).

When Y is NA (i.e. for my prediction dataframe) I have used the unadjusted E that is estimated for the mesh.

Is that likely to cause the precision matrix to be numerical singular?

Many thanks,

James

On 4 Nov 2019, at 13:50, Finn Lindgren <finn.l...@gmail.com> wrote:

Looks like you’re using the wrong E value. I think you intended to use the “exposure” variable from the stack data (extract with inla.stack.data() before the inla call to make that more easily accessible). If this is a LGCP likelihood, I.e. with observations and exposure setup to construct a Cox point process likelihood, then it may be clearer to split into three sub stacks; one with y=1, one with y=0, and one with y=NA that only deals with the prediction.

Finn

On 31 Oct 2019, at 16:56, James Grecian <jamesg...@gmail.com> wrote:

﻿
Hi INLA users,

I am fitting a space-time log Gaussian Cox process model with covariates and am coming unstuck when trying to generate spatial predictions. I would like to generate a lot of predictions from this model, somewhere in the region of 24 different spatial predictions of the entire mesh.

Following the INLA tutorials I have tried to generate spatial predictions while fitting the model. I have appended a dataframe of covariate values from which I want to generate predictions and have included a column of NAs for the Y/ Frequency column. I have also specified link = 1 and compute = TRUE in the `control.predictor` argument.

The model runs fine when there is no prediction data, but when I include the NAs I get the following error:

Function: GMRFLib_factorise_sparse_matrix_TAUCS(), Line: 876, Thread: 0
Fail to factorize Q. I will try to fix it...

Can anyone shed light on why I might be getting this error?

Following this post: http://www.r-inla.org/events/problemswithopenblas I have tried `inla.setOption(mkl = TRUE) but this does not resolve the issue.

Alternatively, given that I am planning on generating so many predicted surfaces should I try an alternative method to generate predictions? For example by sampling from the posterior instead?

Any help would be greatly appreciated!

Many thanks,

James


Here is my model set up. I am working on a Windows server with 44 cores and 512GB memory.

A.st <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh = smesh,
                         loc = smesh$loc[agg.dat$area, ],

                            n.spde = barrier.model$f$n,
                            n.group = k)

stk <- inla.stack(data = list(y = agg.dat$Freq,
                              exposure = agg.dat$exp_adj),
                  A = list(A.st, 1),
                  effects = list(idx,
                                 list(b0 = rep(1, nrow(agg.dat)),
                                      x_bar = agg.dat$x_bar,
                                      x_bar_c_s = agg.dat$x_bar_c_s,
                                      x_bar_c_s_m = agg.dat$x_bar_c_s_m,
                                      x_res_smy = agg.dat$x_res_smy)))

pcrho <- list(theta = list(prior = 'pccor1', param = c(.7, .7)))

f_1 <- y ~ -1 + b0 + x_bar + x_bar_c_s + x_bar_c_s_m + x_res_smy +
  f(s,
    model = barrier.model,

    replicate = s.repl,

                         hyper = pcrho))

m_1 <- inla(f_1,

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Generating predictions from a space-time LGCP model
parts:
That sounds more like a regular geolocated Poisson _count_ model to me, but perhaps the integration weights and 0/1 values are hiding I setup code you didn’t quote?

Finn

On 4 Nov 2019, at 16:41, James Grecian <jamesg...@gmail.com> wrote:

﻿Hi Finn,

You’re right this is an LGCP likelihood. I have a column for observations (Y) and a column for exposure. However I have different numbers of individuals sampled in each period, so the exposure has been adjusted to account for this effect (exp_adj).

When Y is NA (i.e. for my prediction dataframe) I have used the unadjusted E that is estimated for the mesh.

Is that likely to cause the precision matrix to be numerical singular?

Many thanks,

James


On 4 Nov 2019, at 13:50, Finn Lindgren <finn.l...@gmail.com> wrote:

Looks like you’re using the wrong E value. I think you intended to use the “exposure” variable from the stack data (extract with inla.stack.data() before the inla call to make that more easily accessible). If this is a LGCP likelihood, I.e. with observations and exposure setup to construct a Cox point process likelihood, then it may be clearer to split into three sub stacks; one with y=1, one with y=0, and one with y=NA that only deals with the prediction.

Finn

On 31 Oct 2019, at 16:56, James Grecian <jamesg...@gmail.com> wrote:

﻿
Hi INLA users,

I am fitting a space-time log Gaussian Cox process model with covariates and am coming unstuck when trying to generate spatial predictions. I would like to generate a lot of predictions from this model, somewhere in the region of 24 different spatial predictions of the entire mesh.

Following the INLA tutorials I have tried to generate spatial predictions while fitting the model. I have appended a dataframe of covariate values from which I want to generate predictions and have included a column of NAs for the Y/ Frequency column. I have also specified link = 1 and compute = TRUE in the `control.predictor` argument.

The model runs fine when there is no prediction data, but when I include the NAs I get the following error:

file: smtp-taucs.c  hgid: 0bed76828f01  date: Tue Sep 03 11:21:49 2019 +0300
Function: GMRFLib_factorise_sparse_matrix_TAUCS(), Line: 876, Thread: 0
Fail to factorize Q. I will try to fix it...

Can anyone shed light on why I might be getting this error?

Following this post: http://www.r-inla.org/events/problemswithopenblas I have tried `inla.setOption(mkl = TRUE) but this does not resolve the issue.

Alternatively, given that I am planning on generating so many predicted surfaces should I try an alternative method to generate predictions? For example by sampling from the posterior instead?

Any help would be greatly appreciated!

Many thanks,

James


Here is my model set up. I am working on a Windows server with 44 cores and 512GB memory.

A.st <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh = smesh,
                         loc = smesh$loc[agg.dat$area, ],

                         n.group = k,

                            n.spde = barrier.model$f$n,
                            n.group = k)

stk <- inla.stack(data = list(y = agg.dat$Freq,
                              exposure = agg.dat$exp_adj),
                  A = list(A.st, 1),
                  effects = list(idx,
                                 list(b0 = rep(1, nrow(agg.dat)),
                                      x_bar = agg.dat$x_bar,
                                      x_bar_c_s = agg.dat$x_bar_c_s,
                                      x_bar_c_s_m = agg.dat$x_bar_c_s_m,
                                      x_res_smy = agg.dat$x_res_smy)))

pcrho <- list(theta = list(prior = 'pccor1', param = c(.7, .7)))

f_1 <- y ~ -1 + b0 + x_bar + x_bar_c_s + x_bar_c_s_m + x_res_smy +
  f(s,
    model = barrier.model,

    replicate = s.repl,

m_1 <- inla(f_1,

On 4 Nov 2019, at 16:56, Finn Lindgren <finn.l...@gmail.com> wrote:

That sounds more like a regular geolocated Poisson _count_ model to me, but perhaps the integration weights and 0/1 values are hiding I setup code you didn’t quote?

Finn

On 4 Nov 2019, at 16:41, James Grecian <jamesg...@gmail.com> wrote:

﻿Hi Finn,

You’re right this is an LGCP likelihood. I have a column for observations (Y) and a column for exposure. However I have different numbers of individuals sampled in each period, so the exposure has been adjusted to account for this effect (exp_adj).

When Y is NA (i.e. for my prediction dataframe) I have used the unadjusted E that is estimated for the mesh.

Is that likely to cause the precision matrix to be numerical singular?

Many thanks,

James


On 4 Nov 2019, at 13:50, Finn Lindgren <finn.l...@gmail.com> wrote:

Looks like you’re using the wrong E value. I think you intended to use the “exposure” variable from the stack data (extract with inla.stack.data() before the inla call to make that more easily accessible). If this is a LGCP likelihood, I.e. with observations and exposure setup to construct a Cox point process likelihood, then it may be clearer to split into three sub stacks; one with y=1, one with y=0, and one with y=NA that only deals with the prediction.

Finn

On 31 Oct 2019, at 16:56, James Grecian <jamesg...@gmail.com> wrote:

﻿
Hi INLA users,

I am fitting a space-time log Gaussian Cox process model with covariates and am coming unstuck when trying to generate spatial predictions. I would like to generate a lot of predictions from this model, somewhere in the region of 24 different spatial predictions of the entire mesh.

Following the INLA tutorials I have tried to generate spatial predictions while fitting the model. I have appended a dataframe of covariate values from which I want to generate predictions and have included a column of NAs for the Y/ Frequency column. I have also specified link = 1 and compute = TRUE in the `control.predictor` argument.

The model runs fine when there is no prediction data, but when I include the NAs I get the following error:

file: smtp-taucs.c  hgid: 0bed76828f01  date: Tue Sep 03 11:21:49 2019 +0300
Function: GMRFLib_factorise_sparse_matrix_TAUCS(), Line: 876, Thread: 0
Fail to factorize Q. I will try to fix it...

Can anyone shed light on why I might be getting this error?

Following this post: http://www.r-inla.org/events/problemswithopenblas I have tried `inla.setOption(mkl = TRUE) but this does not resolve the issue.

Alternatively, given that I am planning on generating so many predicted surfaces should I try an alternative method to generate predictions? For example by sampling from the posterior instead?

Any help would be greatly appreciated!

Many thanks,

James


Here is my model set up. I am working on a Windows server with 44 cores and 512GB memory.

A.st <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh = smesh,
                         loc = smesh$loc[agg.dat$area, ],
                         group = agg.dat$season,
                         n.group = k,
                         mesh.group = tmesh)

idx <- inla.spde.make.index(name = 's',
                            n.spde = barrier.model$f$n,
                            n.group = k)

stk <- inla.stack(data = list(y = agg.dat$Freq,
                              exposure = agg.dat$exp_adj),
                  A = list(A.st, 1),
                  effects = list(idx,
                                 list(b0 = rep(1, nrow(agg.dat)),
                                      x_bar = agg.dat$x_bar,
                                      x_bar_c_s = agg.dat$x_bar_c_s,
                                      x_bar_c_s_m = agg.dat$x_bar_c_s_m,
                                      x_res_smy = agg.dat$x_res_smy)))

pcrho <- list(theta = list(prior = 'pccor1', param = c(.7, .7)))

f_1 <- y ~ -1 + b0 + x_bar + x_bar_c_s + x_bar_c_s_m + x_res_smy +
  f(s,
    model = barrier.model,
    group = s.group,
    replicate = s.repl,
    control.group = list(model = 'ar1',
                         hyper = pcrho))

m_1 <- inla(f_1,
            family = 'poisson', 
            data = inla.stack.data(stk),
            control.predictor = list(A = inla.stack.A(stk),
                                     link = 1,

parts:
In the LGCP likelihood setup, all rows with Freq=1 should have
exposure=0, and all exposure>0 rows should have Freq=0, some something
isn't right with the LGCP likelihood setup. (all rows shown have _both
Freq and exposure = 1.

Finn

On Wed, 6 Nov 2019 at 14:48, James Grecian <jamesg...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi Finn,
>
> I’ve calculated integration weights based on the code in section 4 of the SPDE book. I didn’t include the whole code as it’s quite long. Here’s a clip from the data frame that is being fed to INLA. Y is Freq and E is adj_exp.
>

parts:
Also notable is that the exposure column is completely different from
the exp_adj column, even though in the stack call you set exposure to
exp_adj.

Finn

> > ﻿Hi Finn,

> > You’re right this is an LGCP likelihood. I have a column for observations (Y) and a column for exposure. However I have different numbers of individuals sampled in each period, so the exposure has been adjusted to account for this effect (exp_adj).

> >
> > Looks like you’re using the wrong E value. I think you intended to use the “exposure” variable from the stack data (extract with inla.stack.data() before the inla call to make that more easily accessible). If this is a LGCP likelihood, I.e. with observations and exposure setup to construct a Cox point process likelihood, then it may be clearer to split into three sub stacks; one with y=1, one with y=0, and one with y=NA that only deals with the prediction.

I have appended a dataframe of covariate values from which I want to generate predictions and have included a column of NAs for the Y/ Frequency column. messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Generating predictions from a space-time LGCP model
parts:
Hi Finn,

Thanks for highlighting this. I hadn’t realised this was required in an LGCP model.

My particular analysis is for a space-time LGCP model and so I’ve been basing my code on section 8.4 of the spde book. The data frame matches the structure of the data frame passed to INLA in section 8.4.

Can you recommend another source of R code for structuring space-time LGCP models?

Best,

James

>
> In the LGCP likelihood setup, all rows with Freq=1 should have
> exposure=0, and all exposure>0 rows should have Freq=0, some something
> isn't right with the LGCP likelihood setup. (all rows shown have _both
> Freq and exposure = 1.
>
> Finn

>>
>> ﻿Hi Finn,
>>
>> You’re right this is an LGCP likelihood. I have a column for observations (Y) and a column for exposure. However I have different numbers of individuals sampled in each period, so the exposure has been adjusted to account for this effect (exp_adj).
>>
>> When Y is NA (i.e. for my prediction dataframe) I have used the unadjusted E that is estimated for the mesh.
>>
>> Is that likely to cause the precision matrix to be numerical singular?
>>
>> Many thanks,
>>
>> James
>>
>>
>> On 4 Nov 2019, at 13:50, Finn Lindgren <finn.l...@gmail.com> wrote:
>>
>> Looks like you’re using the wrong E value. I think you intended to use the “exposure” variable from the stack data (extract with inla.stack.data() before the inla call to make that more easily accessible). If this is a LGCP likelihood, I.e. with observations and exposure setup to construct a Cox point process likelihood, then it may be clearer to split into three sub stacks; one with y=1, one with y=0, and one with y=NA that only deals with the prediction.
>>
>> Finn
>>
>> On 31 Oct 2019, at 16:56, James Grecian <jamesg...@gmail.com> wrote:
>>
>> ﻿

>>
>> Following the INLA tutorials I have tried to generate spatial predictions while fitting the model. I have appended a dataframe of covariate values from which I want to generate predictions and have included a column of NAs for the Y/ Frequency column. I have also specified link = 1 and compute = TRUE in the `control.predictor` argument.
>>

>>
>> Alternatively, given that I am planning on generating so many predicted surfaces should I try an alternative method to generate predictions? For example by sampling from the posterior instead?

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Generating predictions from a space-time LGCP model
parts:
Sec 8.4 aggregates the points into counts for a dual mesh, which turns the continuous Point process model into a discrete count model, via a zero-order integration approximation. The general LGCP likelihood approximation doesn’t do that.

Finn

> On 11 Nov 2019, at 15:36, James Grecian <jamesg...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> ﻿Hi Finn,
>
> Thanks for highlighting this. I hadn’t realised this was required in an LGCP model.
>
> My particular analysis is for a space-time LGCP model and so I’ve been basing my code on section 8.4 of the spde book. The data frame matches the structure of the data frame passed to INLA in section 8.4.
>
> Can you recommend another source of R code for structuring space-time LGCP models?
>
> Best,
>
> James
>
>

>> Finn

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Generating predictions from a space-time LGCP model
parts:
Hi Finn,

So is the model in 8.4 not a space-time LGCP?

Could this be why I’m running into singular matrix issues when generating predictions?

Best,

James

> On 11 Nov 2019, at 15:50, Finn Lindgren <finn.l...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Sec 8.4 aggregates the points into counts for a dual mesh, which turns the continuous Point process model into a discrete count model, via a zero-order integration approximation. The general LGCP likelihood approximation doesn’t do that.
>
> Finn
>
>> On 11 Nov 2019, at 15:36, James Grecian <jamesg...@gmail.com> wrote:
>>
>> ﻿Hi Finn,
>>
>> Thanks for highlighting this. I hadn’t realised this was required in an LGCP model.
>>
>> My particular analysis is for a space-time LGCP model and so I’ve been basing my code on section 8.4 of the spde book. The data frame matches the structure of the data frame passed to INLA in section 8.4.
>>
>> Can you recommend another source of R code for structuring space-time LGCP models?
>>
>> Best,
>>
>> James
>>
>>
>>> On 6 Nov 2019, at 14:56, Finn Lindgren <finn.l...@gmail.com> wrote:
>>>
>>> In the LGCP likelihood setup, all rows with Freq=1 should have
>>> exposure=0, and all exposure>0 rows should have Freq=0, some something
>>> isn't right with the LGCP likelihood setup. (all rows shown have _both
>>> Freq and exposure = 1.
>>>
>>> Finn
>>>

>>>> ﻿Hi Finn,
>>>>
>>>> You’re right this is an LGCP likelihood. I have a column for observations (Y) and a column for exposure. However I have different numbers of individuals sampled in each period, so the exposure has been adjusted to account for this effect (exp_adj).
>>>>
>>>> When Y is NA (i.e. for my prediction dataframe) I have used the unadjusted E that is estimated for the mesh.
>>>>
>>>> Is that likely to cause the precision matrix to be numerical singular?
>>>>
>>>> Many thanks,
>>>>
>>>> James
>>>>
>>>>
>>>>> On 4 Nov 2019, at 13:50, Finn Lindgren <finn.l...@gmail.com> wrote:
>>>>
>>>> Looks like you’re using the wrong E value. I think you intended to use the “exposure” variable from the stack data (extract with inla.stack.data() before the inla call to make that more easily accessible). If this is a LGCP likelihood, I.e. with observations and exposure setup to construct a Cox point process likelihood, then it may be clearer to split into three sub stacks; one with y=1, one with y=0, and one with y=NA that only deals with the prediction.
>>>>
>>>> Finn
>>>>

>>>>
>>>> ﻿
>>>> Hi INLA users,
>>>>
>>>> I am fitting a space-time log Gaussian Cox process model with covariates and am coming unstuck when trying to generate spatial predictions. I would like to generate a lot of predictions from this model, somewhere in the region of 24 different spatial predictions of the entire mesh.
>>>>

I have appended a dataframe of covariate values from which I want to generate predictions and have included a column of NAs for the Y/ Frequency column. messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Generating predictions from a space-time LGCP model
parts:
It’s more a philosophical interpretation issue. It is a valid approximation of an LGCP model. And it’s one that may even be easier to get to be numerically stable that the closer, but more involved, approximations. So no, that is not likely to be the cause of prediction numerical problems.

Finn

> On 11 Nov 2019, at 17:17, James Grecian <jamesg...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> ﻿Hi Finn,
>
> So is the model in 8.4 not a space-time LGCP?
>
> Could this be why I’m running into singular matrix issues when generating predictions?
>
> Best,
>
> James
>
>> On 11 Nov 2019, at 15:50, Finn Lindgren <finn.l...@gmail.com> wrote:
>>
>> Sec 8.4 aggregates the points into counts for a dual mesh, which turns the continuous Point process model into a discrete count model, via a zero-order integration approximation. The general LGCP likelihood approximation doesn’t do that.
>>
>> Finn
>>

>>>

>>> My particular analysis is for a space-time LGCP model and so I’ve been basing my code on section 8.4 of the spde book. The data frame matches the structure of the data frame passed to INLA in section 8.4.
>>>
>>> Can you recommend another source of R code for structuring space-time LGCP models?
>>>
>>> Best,
>>>
>>> James
>>>
>>>

Hi Finn,

Ok, thanks for your insights.

Best,

James

> On 11 Nov 2019, at 17:36, Finn Lindgren <finn.l...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> It’s more a philosophical interpretation issue. It is a valid approximation of an LGCP model. And it’s one that may even be easier to get to be numerically stable that the closer, but more involved, approximations. So no, that is not likely to be the cause of prediction numerical problems.
>
> Finn
>
>> On 11 Nov 2019, at 17:17, James Grecian <jamesg...@gmail.com> wrote:
>>
>> ﻿Hi Finn,
>>
>> So is the model in 8.4 not a space-time LGCP?
>>
>> Could this be why I’m running into singular matrix issues when generating predictions?
>>
>> Best,
>>
>> James
>>
>>> On 11 Nov 2019, at 15:50, Finn Lindgren <finn.l...@gmail.com> wrote:
>>>
>>> Sec 8.4 aggregates the points into counts for a dual mesh, which turns the continuous Point process model into a discrete count model, via a zero-order integration approximation. The general LGCP likelihood approximation doesn’t do that.
>>>
>>> Finn
>>>
>>>>> On 11 Nov 2019, at 15:36, James Grecian <jamesg...@gmail.com> wrote:
>>>>
>>>> ﻿Hi Finn,
>>>>
>>>> Thanks for highlighting this. I hadn’t realised this was required in an LGCP model.
>>>>
>>>> My particular analysis is for a space-time LGCP model and so I’ve been basing my code on section 8.4 of the spde book. The data frame matches the structure of the data frame passed to INLA in section 8.4.
>>>>
>>>> Can you recommend another source of R code for structuring space-time LGCP models?
>>>>
>>>> Best,
>>>>
>>>> James
>>>>
>>>>

>>>>>>
>>>>>> Looks like you’re using the wrong E value. I think you intended to use the “exposure” variable from the stack data (extract with inla.stack.data() before the inla call to make that more easily accessible). If this is a LGCP likelihood, I.e. with observations and exposure setup to construct a Cox point process likelihood, then it may be clearer to split into three sub stacks; one with y=1, one with y=0, and one with y=NA that only deals with the prediction.

messages.author: 66ed4f72a898a51c
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Generating predictions from a space-time LGCP model
parts: > Sec 8.4 aggregates the points into counts for a dual mesh, which turns the continuous Point process model into a discrete count model, via a zero-order integration approximation. The general LGCP likelihood approximation doesn’t do that.

This example in the book was motivated to face issues with large data.
At the time it was written we haven't yet the 'adaptive' strategy
available in INLA. Now, one can avoid the 'binding' approach of
aggregating data into dual mesh polygons for large point process data by
considering control.inla(strategy='adaptive'). Furthermore, the examples
on LGCP in the book and fancier ones can be easier done with the inlabru
package.

Elias

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Generating predictions from a space-time LGCP model
parts:
Note: inlabru doesn’t yet support rgeneric models properly, so while lgcp models are easier with inlabru, one cannot at the moment combine them with barrier-SPDE models. I aim to sort that out in the development version soon.

Finn

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Generating predictions from a space-time LGCP model
parts:
All you need it to use the posterior for lambda you've got from INLA in an algorithm that samples from a LGCP model. For example, you can use lambda samples from the inla.posterior.sample(). The R code int http://www.r-inla.org/examples/case-studies/simpson2011 contain functions that may be useful.

Elias
